learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and abilities to apply graphic engineering techniques.

syllabus_topics: General concepts: Industrial drawing. Graphic expression and CAD in Engineering (3D). Systems used in industrial drawing. Standardization in industrial drawing.

Process Diagrams: Types of diagrams. Elaboration of flow diagrams. Piping and instrumentation diagrams. Installations and symbology (electrical, electronic, hydraulic...). Electrical schematic symbology. Explanatory circuit diagram. Execution of explanatory circuit diagrams.
Assembly and exploded views in industrial drawing: Representations of several elements. Material designation. Surface conditions.
Dimensioning. Functional and manufacturing-based dimensioning. Tolerances and fits: Dimensional tolerances. Fits. Geometric tolerances. Functional dimensioning.

Detachable fastening elements. Threads and threaded connections. Keys and keyways. Transformation of movement by means of threaded connections. Bolts. Studs. Washers. Pins. Locking of screws and nuts. Permanent fastening elements (adhesives, welds, rivets...).

Power transmission elements (gears, pulleys and belts, chains...). Bearings (bushings, rolling bearings...). Piping elements (flanges, elbows, fastenings...). Types of pipe plans. Use in piping and fittings design.
Specific 2D CAD design. Symbology libraries. 2D perspectives and isometric views.

3D Design: 3D work environment. Coordinate systems and work planes in 3D. 3D visualization. Creation of surfaces in AutoCAD. Creation of surface meshes and volumes. Creation of solids in AutoCAD: basic solids, extrude command, revolve, etc. Boolean operations. 3D operations. Editing 3D solids.
assessment_rules: The overall weighted average must be greater than 5.0 to pass the course. A minimum grade of 4.5 is required for the written theoretical-practical test and the practical CAD software test. Non-re-evaluable activities (lab practices and group work) cannot exceed 40% of the global grade. Students failing or not presenting in the ordinary call may re-evaluate only the re-evaluable activities in the extraordinary call. Unjustified absence from more than 30% of practices will result in a 0 for the practice block and failing the course.
